TOWN OF LUNENBURG
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
P.O. BOX 135
LUNENBURG, MA. 01462
Minutes from the Board of Assessors meeting held: July 7, 2015
The meeting opened at 5:45 pm.
Present: Chairman, Louis Franco, Board Members, Matt Papini, Sr.,
Richard Letarte, Associate Assessor, George Bourgault and Louise Paquette, Administrative Assistant.
Board reviewed and approved current expense vouchers, abatements, warrants, commitments, payroll
and June 2, 2015 minutes.
Louise reported that the FY16 Preliminary Real Estate bills were mailed on June 29t.
". Matt questioned the
outcome of the preliminary estimated tax percentage in regards to elevating the valuation factor within the
Munis tax system. Louise reported that she contacted Munis for assistance regarding the preliminary
assessment ratio adjustment. Munis advised that the preliminary amount percentage could be adjusted
under the tax setting process. She reported that Harald was in communication with the Town Accountant
and once obtaining the FY2016 debt figure associated with the new High School, it was decided that the
preliminary bills be inflated by a factor of 55.12 percent. Matt motioned to reiterate the factor amount of
55.12 percent on the estimated preliminary bills; seconded by Rich. Louise stated that a letter regarding
the update on School Building Project along with information regarding the tax impart was sent to each
taxpayer.
Louise reported that there were no omitted or revised bills in FY15. She stated that at this time of year in
accordance with the provisions of General Laws Chapter 59, Sect. 75, the Board of Assessors submits
the report on the omitted and revised assessments made during the Fiscal Year.
BOA reviewed and approved CAl Technologies, Inc. contract for mapping services for FY2016. It was
noted that the contract expense increased $150.00; costs in FY15 was $2,400. and costs in FY16 is
$2,550. Louise will need to request an adjustment transfer in monies in the FY16 budget to
accommodate this increase.
George spoke with the Board regarding the upcoming ATB case for the property located at 494 West
Townsend Road. The Applicant stated that he believes that the solar farm abutting his property has a
detrimental effect to his value of this property. After much discussion, the Board agreed that Harald &
George should meet with him on-site, review the assessment and come to a resolution / mutual
agreement prior to the ATB meeting.
George stated that he has been working on 2014 sales analysis assessment rations & valuations. He
reported a total of 91 valid sales (arm's length) in 2014 and the sales indicated a 3% Increase in values
on single family homes. He noted that there were 23 condo sales and the condo sale values have
increased approximately 10%. After reviewing the sales analysis report, the BOA approved to accept the
recommendation of valuation increases up to 3% to the single family homes and a 10% valuation
increase on condos.
Next meeting will be held on Tuesday, August 4, 2015 at 5:45 pm.
Meeting adjourned at 7:40 pm.
Respegitully Submitted
alre
coulse Paquette

Update on School Building Project, June 2015
The school building project is approximately 33% complete. The pace-of the project has increased significantly with over 100
workers on the site daily. The number of workers on site will increase into the summer as the work in and outside the building
continues. To date the Town has received reimbursement in the amount of $8,829,589 from the Massachusetts School Building
Authority (MSBA). The new field adjacent to Massachusetts Avenue will be available this fall. The binder for the east roadway is
scheduled to be laid this month. Site work during the summer will impact both the LHS and TCP campus roadways and parking. The
public will be notified of detours or closures on school grounds as necessary throughout the summer.
In Area "A" where the high school classrooms and
the library are located, exterior framing, blocking,
sheathing and roof installation is complete. The
spraying of foam insulation, air and vapor barrier is
nearing completion. Brick veneer will soon be
underway. The slab-on-deck and slab-on-grade are
complete in Area A. Interior framing on the first
floor is complete and underway on the second floor.
Plumbing, mechanical, electrical ductwork, and pipe
installation is on-going.
Area / Building D
Area/Building C
Area/Building B
Area A/Building 8
In Areas "B" & "C", where the auditorium,
administrative offices, art and music classrooms,
gym and locker rooms are located, the slab-on-grade
and slab-on-deck is complete for the office, second
floor classrooms and upper and lower corridors.
Masonry work in the auditorium is near completion
and continues in the gym and locker rooms. The
auditorium and the remaining music classroom area
are being prepared for the slab-on-grade pour.
Exterior framing, blocking, sheathing, and roof
installation is on-going.
Mechanical, electrical and
plumbing hangers are underway.
Finally, in Area "D", where the middle school
classrooms and cafeteria are located, the roof
installation is near completion. The slab-on-deck
and slab-on-grade are nearly complete with only the
kitchen and cafeteria remaining to be completed.
Fireproofing in the classroom wing portion of Area D
is completed. Exterior framing, blocking and
sheathing is underway. Interior framing, plumbing,
mechanical,
electrical ductwork, and pipe
installation will begin mid-June.
The building project has its own webpage (lunenburgschools.net/school-building-project/) on the District's website
(www.lunenburgschools.net) and a Facebook page-Lunenburg Middle/High School Building Project.
The new school is on schedule to open in August, 2016. Detailed planning for the transition to the new building
and the reconfigured district is underway.
Update on Tax Impact: Your First Quarter FY2016 Tax Bill includes an additional amount for the new High School/
Middle School Construction Project. The Town's share of this project, net of the grant the Town has received from
the MA School Building Authority, is approximately $35M. To date, the Town has borrowed $29,605,000, the
associated debt service of which now appears on your property tax bill.
The FY2016 tax impact of this project on the average homeowner is: $351.26
The impact to your individual tax bill depends upon your property's Actual Assessed Valuation. The Average
Assessed Valuation in Lunenburg for FY2015 is: $246,347. (Please note, the Average Assessed Valuation for
FY2016 is not calculated until the Q3 Tax Bills are prepared.)
The Town expects to borrow the remainder of the Town's share of the project costs, about an additional $5M, in
January 2016. The debt service costs for this additional amount should appear on your FY2017 Tax Bill.
